annotations.text: Three directions for the real Syncophant UI — same Home screen, same data, three worlds. Researched from Vercel's Geist system, Linear's redesign, and the soft-native Mac school (Things/Transmit). Pick one; the winner gets all six screens rebuilt in its language, then implemented in the app.

A — INK (Geist school)
Paper & ink: no brand color at all — typography and hairlines do everything; status dots are the only chroma. Mono uppercase as the 'console voice', keyboard-first hints.
Why: the most unique of the three in 2026; reads like a beautifully typeset manifest — perfect for a tool about files.
Tradeoff: austere; can feel empty or cold if content is sparse. Dark variant needs care.

B — CARBON (Linear school)
Near-black machined surfaces, hairline borders, low font weights, one electric teal used like a flashlight (action + progress only). ⌘K command bar, glowing active row.
Why: fits a tray-resident background daemon; dark-first suits dev desks; our mono paths already belong here.
Tradeoff: the most-imitated look in dev tools right now — distinctive execution required, or it reads generic. Light mode is the afterthought.

C — NATIVE (Things/Transmit school)
Soft mac-native: real sidebar, white cards on warm gray, gentle depth, system type. The 'invisible tool' philosophy — the app disappears into macOS.
Why: lowest-friction familiarity; calm; ages well.
Tradeoff: the least unique — you asked for distinctive, and this is deliberately quiet. Also the hardest to keep consistent on Windows/Linux later.

Syncophant — static mockups, v2
Utilitarian pass: sharp corners, Space Grotesk + Geist Mono, teal on cool slate.

Superseded pending the direction pick on page 1.
